items.title: BNC Notice & Service Disruption
items.content_text:
Thursday, October 15, 2026
The Bankruptcy Noticing Center (BNC) has been experiencing a nationwide service disruption since on or about October 9, 2026, affecting all U.S. Bankruptcy Courts. The outage has interrupted the BNC's processing and delivery of notices and orders issued by the Court. As a result, parties who ordinarily receive notices and orders through the BNC may experience delays in receiving those documents. The outage is also affecting CM/ECF users' ability to generate and print a List of Creditors.
The outage does not affect the electronic delivery of Notices of Electronic Filing (NEFs), which continue to be generated and distributed normally through CM/ECF.
At this time, there is no estimated date or time for restoration of services.
Additionally, the following websites are unavailable:
bnc.uscourts.gov
bankruptcynotices.uscourts.gov
notices.uscourts.gov
National Creditor Registration Service website that supports CM/ECF access to address labels
The Court will provide additional updates as information becomes available.

items.title: Digital Archive Services
items.content_text:
Open Access
- the online digital collection of the Maine State Archives
Welcome to the online digital collection of the Maine State Archives. These records include bills introduced in the Legislature, reports from the Governor's Executive Council, election returns, deeds and maps from the Maine Land Office, vital statistics prior to 1892, federal census records up to 1880, county court records dating back to 1636, and military records through World War I, among others. As of March 1, 2026, our online collection includes over one million individual records. The Maine State Archives will continue to expand this database as we digitize more of our collection. All documents are public records and are free to download.

STATE OF MAINE 
SUPREME JUDICIAL COURT 
AMENDMENT TO 
MAINE RULES OF UNIFIED CRIMINAL PROCEDURE 
 
2026 Me. Rules 03 
 
Effective: October 1, 2026 
 
 All of the Justices concurring therein, the following amendment to the 
Maine Rules of Unified Criminal Procedure is adopted to be effective on the date 
indicated above.  The specific amendment  is stated below.  To aid in the 
understanding of the amendment, an Advisory Note appears after the text of 
the amendment.  The Advisory Note states the reason for recommending the 
amendment, but the Advisory Note is not part of the amendment adopted by 
the Court. 
 
 1. Rule 4A of the  Maine Rules of Unified Criminal  Procedure is 
amended to read as follows: 
 
RULE 4A.  PROBABLE CAUSE DETERMINATION UPON WARRANTLESS 
ARREST FOR ANY CRIME 
 
(a) Timing: Required Findings.   Except in a bona fide emergency or 
other extraordinary circumstance, when a defendant arrested without a 
warrant for any crime is not released from custody within 48 hours after arrest, 
including Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays, the court or justi ce of the 
peace shall determine, within that time period, whether there is probable cause 
to believe that a crime has been committed and that the arrested defendant has 
committed it.  If the evidence does not establish such probable cause, the court 
or jus tice of the peace shall discharge the arrested defendant.  If a probable 
cause determination has not taken place within 36 hours after the arrest, 
including Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays, the custodian shall notify the 
attorney for the State of the upcoming deadline.  For purposes of this Rule 
“custody” means incarceration. Rule 45(a) and (b) have no application to this 
subdivision. 
(b) Evidence.  In making this determination the court or justice of the 
peace shall consider:

Maine Department of Labor announces October workplace safety and labor law training schedule

September 24, 2026

For Immediate Release: Thursday, Sept. 24, 2026

Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist media.dol@maine.gov

AUGUSTA - The Maine Department of Labor offers free workplace safety and labor law training to help employers, managers, supervisors, human resources professionals and others understand workplace safety requirements and Maine labor laws. The Department has announced its schedule of October classes, with trainings offered through SafetyWorks! and the Bureau of Labor Standards.

Registration is required, and space may be limited. View the October schedule and register for a class.

Unless otherwise noted, classes are held at the SafetyWorks! Training Institute at the Maine Department of Labor, 45 Commerce Drive in Augusta.

October Class Schedule

Fire Extinguisher/Emergency Action Plans/Workplace Violence Thursday, Oct. 1, 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.
SafetyWorks! Training Institute, Augusta

Workplace emergencies include fire, medical, and workplace violence. This course covers the requirements of an emergency action plan, fire extinguisher use, and considering the potential for workplace violence. The SWTI Lab includes a fire extinguisher discharge activity to assist participants in learning how to use a fire extinguisher.

Bloodborne Pathogens Train-the-Trainer Friday, Oct. 2, 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. SafetyWorks! Training Institute, Augusta

This half-day class provides guidance on what is needed to be compliant with the bloodborne pathogen standard. This course will review written program requirements, training, documentation, Hepatitis B, and sharp logs.

Safety & Health Management Systems Tuesday, Oct. 6, 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. SafetyWorks! Training Institute, Augusta

Successful safety and health programs are more than just compliance with the OSHA standards. Injuries and illnesses are reduced when employers possess common elements to identify and address safety and health hazards. This course outlines roles and responsibilities, common principles, required functions and programs of a successful safety and health management system. This course prepares organizations who would like to pursue SHARP/ SHAPE.

Cold & Heat Illness Prevention Friday, Oct. 9, 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.
SafetyWorks! Training Institute, Augusta

Whether your employees work outside or inside, cold and hot temperatures can be hazardous to their health. This class covers cold and heat temperature illnesses, signs and symptoms, and control measures to prevent and treat temperature related injuries.

Welding/Compressed Gas Tuesday, Oct. 13, 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.
SafetyWorks! Training Institute, Augusta

This class covers the requirements of the welding standard, in addition to the storage and proper use of compressed gas. Proper inspection techniques of hoses, torches, and regulators will be demonstrated.

Wage & Hour Compliance Wednesday, Oct. 14, 9 a.m. to noon Maine Department of Health & Human Services, 200 Main St, Conference Room A, Lewiston

This course is designed for human resource or benefits professionals, accountants, business owners, managers, or payroll supervisors. Labor laws can be complex.
